newsitem.title: USA: GM December N.A. output down from year ago. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: GM December N.A. output down from year ago. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]

text.p: General Motors Corp said Monday it produced 363,000 cars and trucks in North America during the month of December 1996, down 8.3 percent from the 396,000 vehicles GM built in December 1995.
GM also said its first quarter 1997 production forecast for the United States, Canada and Mexico remains at 1,413,000 vehicles, unchanged from estimates released a month ago.

The first quarter total represents a 15.9 percent increase from the 1,219,000 cars and trucks produced in the first quarter of 1996. (Corrects from "...a 18.6 percent increase from the 1,191,000 cars...)

GM plans to build 761,000 passenger cars in North America during the the first quarter of 1997, compared with 681,000 a year earlier. GM's North American truck production for the first quarter is estimated at 652,000 units, compared to the 538,000 trucks it built a year ago.
In the fourth quarter of 1996, GM said it produced a total of 1,191,000 cars in the United States, Canada and Mexico, down 13.2 percent from the 1,372,000 vehicles built in the same period of 1995.

GM's fourth quarter North American passenger car production was down 21.7 percent, or 176,000 units, from the year-earlier period to 636,000 cars, while North American truck production fell 0.9 percent, or 5,000 units, to 555,000 trucks.
